classification.difficultyReason: Arrange six whole numbers subject to nine simultaneous restrictions on consecutive values.

content.prompt: Place the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 in the circles of the following figure so that no two adjacent numbers (that is, numbers with a difference of 1) are connected by a line.

spec.description: Two inner vertical columns with outward middle circles. All nine source connections are retained; there is no top-left to bottom-right diagonal. Decorative blue strokes become ordinary black strokes.
spec.mathematics: Vertices TL, TR, ML, MR, BL, BR; edges TL–TR, TL–ML, ML–BL, TL–BL, TR–MR, MR–BR, TR–BR, BL–BR, BL–TR.
spec.answerVisibility: Six empty circles remain visible in the student question.

answer.short: One solution: top row 4, 1; middle row 2, 5; bottom row 6, 3.
answer.worked:
Put 1 at the top-right and 6 at the bottom-left. These circles have four connections each, so put 2 and 5 in the two outer middle circles, respectively. Put 4 at the top-left and 3 at the bottom-right.

The differences across the nine connected pairs are $3,2,4,2,4,2,2,3,5$. None is 1, so every restriction is satisfied.

spec.description: Complete solution figure with exactly the question's topology and six filled number positions.
spec.mathematics: TL=4, TR=1, ML=2, MR=5, BL=6, BR=3. Every number 1–6 is used once and every connected pair differs by more than 1.
